howto.q: How do I import a website into Figma?
howto.name: Import a website into Figma with PageRecast
howto.intro: Install the Chrome extension and the Figma plugin, then:

capture.name: Capture the page
capture.text: Open the page in Chrome, open the PageRecast side panel, pick the widths and themes, and press Capture.

copy.name: Copy it for Figma
copy.text: Press Copy for Figma, or save a .recast file to share or open later.

paste.name: Paste it in Figma
paste.text: Run the PageRecast plugin, paste with ⌘ V or Ctrl V, check the frames and press Import.

free.a: Yes. There are no plans, limits, trials, accounts or watermarks, and there never will be. PageRecast is open source under the MIT licence.

login.q: Does it work on pages behind a login?
login.a: Yes. The extension captures what your browser shows, so dashboards, admin panels and anything else you are signed in to import like any public page.

localhost.q: Can I import localhost or a staging site?
localhost.a: Yes. Any page that opens in Chrome can be captured, including localhost, staging and preview deployments, with no tunnel and no public URL.

what.q: What does PageRecast import into Figma?
what.a: Frames with their fills, borders, radii, shadows and blur; text with its fonts and inline styles; images; SVG icons as editable vectors; colour variables with Light and Dark modes; text styles; and a locked screenshot beside each frame to compare against.

fonts.q: What happens to the page's fonts?
fonts.a: PageRecast uses every font Figma has, installed on your computer or from Google Fonts. A font Figma doesn't have is replaced by the closest match, and every replacement is listed before and after you import.

autolayout.a: Yes, wherever it fits. Flex layouts become Auto Layout when every child lands within 1.5 px of where the page put it. Everything else keeps its exact position, so the import always looks like the page.

privacy.a: Yes. There is no PageRecast server, no account and no analytics. Captures are built in your browser and stay on your computer. The Figma plugin only downloads the images the page already uses, straight from the sites they belong to.

firefox.a: Yes. PageRecast for Firefox makes the same captures for the same Figma plugin. It captures a page in the theme and language it shows at the moment, so switch those first.

agents.a: Yes. The PageRecast MCP server lets agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Cursor capture pages, read their design tokens and send captures to Figma. It runs on your computer too: npx -y pagerecast-mcp.

screenshot.q: How is this different from a screenshot?
screenshot.a: A screenshot is one flat image. PageRecast rebuilds the page as layers: text you can edit, vectors you can recolour, frames you can resize and colours as variables. The screenshot comes along only as a locked reference.

privacy.title: Privacy policy | PageRecast
privacy.description: PageRecast does not collect, transmit, sell or share any personal data. Everything happens on your computer.
privacy.heading: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: PageRecast is a browser extension for Chrome and Firefox and a Figma plugin, made by Shades Media Group. This policy covers all of them.
privacy.short: PageRecast does not collect, transmit, sell or share any personal data. Everything happens on your computer.
privacy.chromePage: The page you choose to capture. When you press Capture, the extension reads the layout, styles, text and images of the current tab, of a URL you type, or of a URL the Figma plugin sent through our capture page (only that page can ask, and only after you press Capture there), using Chrome's debugger permission. It attaches only for that capture and detaches when it ends.
privacy.chromeTabs: Tab titles, addresses and icons, to show which page will be captured.
privacy.chromeStorage: Local storage on your device, to keep your settings and recent captures. You can delete any capture from the panel; removing the extension deletes all of them.
privacy.chromeNetwork: The extension makes no requests to any server of ours. Images in a capture are read from your browser's cache or loaded the same way the page loads them.
privacy.firefox: The Firefox version accesses the same things, but reads the page with Firefox's tabs and scripting permissions and access to all websites (<all_urls>) instead of the debugger permission. It uses that access only on the tab you capture, to read the page, take its screenshot and load its images. As in Chrome, nothing leaves your device.
privacy.pluginCapture: The capture you paste or open, to build layers in the current Figma file.
privacy.pluginImages: Images referenced by a capture, which it downloads directly from the websites they belong to.
privacy.pluginStorage: Figma's plugin storage, to remember your import settings.
privacy.pluginAgents: Captures an AI agent queued on your computer, only when you turn on agent imports. The plugin collects them from 127.0.0.1, a server on your own machine that the PageRecast MCP server runs, using a pairing code you enter.
privacy.pluginWeb: The plugin's Web tab opens pagerecast.shades.md/capture/ with the page address and settings after the # of the link, a part browsers never send to a server. That page passes them to the extension in your browser, and the capture is copied to your clipboard there.
privacy.data: None. There are no accounts, analytics, crash reports or tracking of any kind.
privacy.children: PageRecast is a design tool and is not directed at children.
privacy.changes: Changes to this policy are published on this page and noted in the changelog.
